evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensors show abrupt decline from 10.66 mg/L at 50.0h to 3.70 mg/L at 52.0h, worst at decision time
P assay at t=48h (available 52h): 2.80 g/L — production ongoing, mass must be retained (stop = zero counted production)

Physical forward model: keep min DO 1.51 (3.6h below 2.0 limit, infeasible); reduce_feed 1.44 (5h below); combined 1.47 (4.6h below); strong_feed_reduction 2.18 (0h below, feasible, 1/5 sensitivity members feasible vs 0 for keep)
Forward model product mass: strong_feed_reduction 240.98 kg > combined 214.24 > reduce_feed 202.16 > keep 197.54
Source batches show DO2 dip to ~8 mg/L at similar phase with natural recovery — but receiving dip is far more severe (~3.7 mg/L and falling), so waiting is not supported
args.rationale: At the 52h decision point the receiving fermenter shows an abrupt, ongoing DO2 collapse (10.66 → 3.70 mg/L within 2h), with the trajectory heading toward the 2.0 mg/L oxygen-constraint floor. Source batches only dipped to ~8 mg/L at the analogous growth phase and recovered; the receiving run is far more severe, indicating much higher oxygen demand (likely from a transfer/scaling difference, model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.51). The source-calibrated forward model shows KEEP would violate the oxygen limit for 3.6h with min DO ~1.51 mg/L (0/5 sensitivity members feasible), reduce_feed and combined still violate (~1.44/1.47 mg/L min). Only strong_feed_reduction (feed×0.6, air×1.15) restores feasibility: min DO 2.18 mg/L, 0h below limit, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible — and it also maximizes product mass (~241 kg vs ~198 kg under KEEP), retaining concentration AND volume (product mass, not concentration alone). Waiting risks an oxygen-constraint violation and possible forced stop (zero counted production). Recommend strong_feed_reduction now.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated estimate, not the hidden evaluator realization; source and receiving processes differ. Sensitivity range for strong_feed_reduction still includes members with min DO as low as 1.30 mg/L (1/5 members infeasible), so residual constraint risk remains; DO2 should be monitored and air further increased or feed cut if DO approaches 2 mg/L. Current DO2 (~3.7 mg/L) is above 2.0, so there is a short window; delay would worsen feasibility.
